one_liner: Compiled C++20 SIMD FFT library (any size, 1-D/N-D, c2c/r2c/DCT); the author's sweep has it 1.34-1.43x faster than single-thread FFTW_MEASURE.
what_it_does: Admiral computes complex and real FFTs of any length and rank in float, double or long double, plus DCT-II/III and DST-II/III, batched strided lines and single-axis transforms. It has three front ends over one compiled engine: a C++ plan API (admiral::plan<T>, plan_r2c, plan_r2r, axis_plan, strides_plan, plus one-shot forward/inverse), a C API (adm_plan_*), and an FFTW-subset shim (<admiral/fftw3.h>) that recompiles existing complex-DFT FFTW code. Data is row-major, last axis fastest. The C++ and C inverses divide by N; the shim keeps FFTW's unscaled convention.
how_it_is_fast: Butterfly codelets up to radix 64 are unrolled at compile time with poet and vectorized with xsimd, and a mixed-radix decimation-in-frequency (DIF) pass chain is scheduled over them. Awkward lengths go to Good-Thomas prime-factor, Rader (prime N) or Bluestein (chirp-z) routes. Out-of-cache sizes use Bailey's four-step algorithm with fused, cache-blocked transposes and non-temporal stores past about 2x L3. A fitted cost model picks the route at plan time (effort::estimate); effort::automatic also times the top candidates. A per-plan thread pool engages only above about 2^15 elements and sizes itself from modelled work plus measured wake cost.
when_to_use: Single-threaded 1-D or N-D complex FFTs in float or double on AVX-512 or AVX2 x86, where you can build with -march for the target
Non-power-of-two and prime lengths that you would otherwise run through FFTW's generic paths: codelets up to 64 plus Rader/Bluestein keep them on SIMD code
Moving existing FFTW complex-DFT code (fftw_plan_dft_*, fftw_execute, fftw_execute_dft, fftwf_ mirror) by recompiling against <admiral/fftw3.h>
Large 2-D/3-D transforms with 16 threads, where the author's sweep shows 2.67x (f64) to 3.53x (f32) over threaded ducc0 for 3-D
Code that wants plan construction without a wisdom or tuning step (estimate mode is deterministic, and fully reproducible with ADM_MEASURE=OFF)
when_not_to_use: Large multi-threaded 1-D transforms: against threaded ducc0 at 16 threads the geomean swings from 0.33x to 1.82x by size (2M and 8M lose by about 3x), because the six-step split rejects some sizes
Code that needs strict IEEE results: the default build adds -ffast-math (reassociation, flushed denormals), so turn ADM_USE_FAST_MATH off and expect less speed
Code that needs FFTW's r2c/r2r, guru, split-complex, wisdom or fftw_plan_with_nthreads through the shim: these calls are not provided and do not compile

Projects that need an OSI-approved license or a mature dependency: BSD-3-Clause-Attribution adds a required acknowledgment line, and the project has no stars, a single author, a 2026 history and an AI-assisted codebase by its own README
Small build machines or quick CI: one engine translation unit peaks near 12 GB of RAM at AVX-512 native, and the README warns that compiles are long

integration.form: shared lib (also static lib), built with CMake 3.25+
integration.dependencies: xsimd and poet (fetched by CPM at configure time); Catch2, ducc0, nanobench and optionally system fftw3/fftw3f only for tests and benchmarks
integration.min_toolchain: C++20 by default (C++17 with -DADM_CXX_STANDARD=17; the two builds are not link-compatible); GCC 14+ or Clang 19+ recommended, older C++20 compilers work but generate slower code
integration.platforms: x86-64 measured (Xeon w5-3435X AVX-512, plus Ice Lake/Rome/Genoa in the author's fft_bench); default -march=native binaries are not portable (use ADM_TARGET_ARCH=x86-64-v3); thread pinning is Linux-only; other ISAs not documented
integration.thread_safety: Documented: forward/inverse on one plan may be called from several threads (all scratch is per call), but pooled calls serialize, so use one plan per thread for throughput; with the FFTW shim, concurrent fftw_execute on one plan races on its planned output buffer, so use fftw_execute_dft with per-thread buffers
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: an FFTW shim covers only complex DFT planning/execution, the alloc helpers and the fftwf_ mirror; flags other than FFTW_ESTIMATE all map to a plan-time race, and failed plans return NULL with no reason

gotchas: nthreads=0 (auto) runs serial below about 32k elements; forcing 16 threads on shapes under about 16k elements is 0.7-1.0x of serial per the benchmark README
effort::automatic/measure pick routes by timing, so plans can differ between runs and machines; one-shot functions always use estimate
Span overloads validate sizes and throw admiral::error subclasses (size_error, unsupported_error, internal_error); pointer overloads trust the caller
long double runs a scalar backend and is limited to plan, plan_r2c and the one-shots; there is no strided r2r, so an N-D DCT needs your own transposes
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Choose Admiral over PocketFFT (C++ branch) and ducc0 when you have AVX2/AVX-512 x86 and can build per-target: its own sweep has it 1.1-2.7x faster than ducc0 single-threaded. Choose it over FFTW when you want a permissive (attribution) license and a recompile-only shim for complex DFTs. VectorFFT (measured against MKL) or FFTW itself are the better choice when you need wisdom, the full guru API or results from someone other than the author.
verified_claims_summary: The author's 2026-08-24 sweep on a 16-core Xeon w5-3435X (GCC 14.2, Release, -march=native, -ffast-math; nanobench minimum time, each size accuracy-gated against a reference DFT) has single-thread Admiral at 1.34x (1-D) and 1.43x (N-D) the speed of system FFTW with FFTW_MEASURE. These are geomeans over 19 lengths and 9 shapes, both precisions pooled; FFTW's version and configure flags are not stated, and no per-size times are published. Against ducc0 c4dda23 it reports 2.18x/2.70x (f64/f32) at 1-D, but there the ducc0 arm allocates its output inside the timed region, so small-N 1-D ratios are inflated.
status_note: Very active (last commit 2026-09-29; CI, codecov, Doxygen/Sphinx docs, 0 open issues). It is a one-author project with no adoption yet, and its BSD-3-Clause-Attribution license is not OSI-approved, so it is catalogued as reference rather than copyable.
